subject: swampTroll

Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module for a Warcraft-style swamp troll model, aiming for a manageable size while nailing the key features: hunched posture, long arms, teal-green skin, tusks, mohawk, pointed ears, and bone fetish accessories.

Working out the swamp platform base with lily pads, a totem, and glowing green fire, plus figuring out approximate height and joint hierarchy -- hips, spine chain, neck, head, jaw, arms angled outward -- while double-checking the builder API's rules around chain naming and span counts so the rig comes out correctly.

I'm plotting the spine path from pelvis through chest to neck and head with a forward-hunched curve, then setting up the torso loft stations bound to that spine chain, treating the hips as the pelvis anchor point the loft projects from.

For the loft stations I'm setting width along X and height along Z depth, defining width/height values at increasing heights up the torso (pelvis, belly, chest) to shape a pot-bellied silhouette.

I'm extending the same body centers into a spine chain (using the torso loft points) and then starting a neck chain running from the shoulders up toward the head.

Using `neck.at(1)` as the parent point makes more sense for referencing the chain's tip. For the troll's head shape—long with a heavy jaw, low brow, big nose—I'll use word-based local directions like forward/up relative to the head joint, since those stay orientation-independent and work cleanly for mirroring left/right sides.

I'll build a helper that maps forward/up/left into local coordinates, then construct the cranium as a scaled sphere positioned via that helper, picking a jungle-troll teal-blue skin tone to match the swamp-troll aesthetic.

Writing skin paint shader...

I'm thinking trolls should have tribal war paint and glowing eyes, so I'll add decals for chest tattoos and glowing yellow eyes projected onto the head geometry.

Worried that decal projection could fail silently if it misses the surface, which risks a crash. A safer alternative might be placing a small flat circle textured with the eye graphic directly at a computed surface point on the scaled ellipsoid head, or embedding a partial sphere as the eyeball itself.

For the troll's eyes, I'll go with glowing embedded spheres (small yellow-orange orbs, radius around 0.032, half-sunk into the head) topped with a tiny flattened dark sphere as the pupil slit -- giving that chunky, no-visible-whites Warcraft look while avoiding decal risk on the face. I'll reserve decals for flatter surfaces like the chest where projection is more reliable, trusting the SDK there for tribal war paint markings.

I'm figuring out decal placement using surface raycasting -- casting a ray from a chosen origin toward the body part to get a hit point and normal, then using that as the decal's anchor, with a null-check fallback since the ray might miss. I plan to build a helper function that wraps this ray-to-decal logic with options for texture, size, and positioning, then apply it for face war paint stripes across the eyes and a tribal glyph on the chest, plus a loincloth pattern using the same SVG-texture approach.

For the cloth flap, I'm deciding to skip texturing and instead paint a zigzag red/ochre pattern directly using surface coordinates on an extruded shape, which avoids texture-mapping headaches. I'm cataloging the remaining decorative elements -- face paint, chest tattoo, feather cards, fire glow cards, and other hanging fetish decorations -- so I can tally how many distinct textures and card types the piece will need.

Now I'm working out the leg structure for the troll: a bowlegged, digitigrade stance with thick thighs, bent knees, and big three-toed feet, using an IK limb setup with hip and ankle target positions to get that hunched Warcraft-troll silhouette.

For toes I'll keep it simple with capsules extending forward from the ankle bone, adding small claw spikes at the tips, using basic joint names per toe.

For legs, I'm sweeping the thigh and shin as one continuous chain with radii tapering from thick at the hip to narrow at the knee, widening slightly for the calf, then tapering again at the ankle. The limb function will take a root, target, segment lengths, and bend direction to return the chain of points.

Looking at bend direction, I'll use the single-vector form like `[0, 0, 1]` matching the example for `limb(hip, foot, [0.3, 0.3], [0, 0, 1])`. For foot placement, I'm setting the ankle around y=0.17 with a flat slab foot beneath it, roughly 0.2 wide, 0.1 thick, and 0.34 long to form the sole resting at y=0.

I'm checking whether the lowest points of feet, toes, and base all align at y=0 so nothing floats or clips through the floor, and considering raising the whole model slightly so a base/mud disc sits at y=0 while the feet rest on top of it rather than sinking in.

I just need absolute coordinates for the skeleton points and ground props, since everything else inherits the shift automatically. Total height works out fine with the mohawk reaching about 2.6 after the offset. For the arms, I'm sketching a long muscular rest pose with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints positioned to make the troll's reach extend down toward knee level, using a catmull curve through those three points.

For the hands, I'm planning a palm box with capsule fingers and a clawed thumb, each finger as its own small joint chain with two spans so the bends read cleanly against the smooth skin blending.

Totaling it all up, I land around sixty joints across spine, neck, head, jaw, arms, fingers, legs, and toes, which feels manageable. For the rest pose, arms hang down with open hands and slightly spread fingers pointing downward, with each finger chain offset from the wrist joint in local model space.

I'm sizing arm segments—upper arm, elbow, forearm, wrist—and designing the shoulder with a deltoid sphere plus pauldrons: a boar-skull/tusk pad on the left and a leather pad with tusks and feathers on the right, both ringed with bone spikes.

Now I'm building the head: cranium ellipsoid, brow ridge, a hooked nose swept from between the eyes to the tip, and a separate jaw joint with a chunky lower jaw and chin, plus curved ivory tusks sprouting upward from it.

I'm also figuring out the mouth and ears — small teeth, an upper lip, and long, pointed troll-style ears that sweep backward and outward, extruded from a flat outline shape oriented to point up-and-back as seen from the front.

Working out the ear outline coordinates...

Finalizing the leaf shape as a non-self-intersecting polygon with slight thickness and beveling, keeping smoothing at zero to preserve the sharp tip. Now moving on to the ear rings, planning a gold torus geometry at the earlobe.

I'm working out head coordinates next, placing the eyes beneath the brow, setting up the jaw joint and aim direction toward the chin, and sketching the lower jaw as a frustum box with careful orientation handling.

Simplifying this, I'll skip rotating the jaw box itself since the jaw bone orientation already handles the tilt, using axis-aligned boxes instead. I'm sizing the lower jaw box and adding a slightly larger jutting chin piece, considering flat shading for a low-poly look.

Now I'm figuring out the tusks using a swept bezier curve along the jaw, tapering from a base radius down to a sharp point, with the base anchored at the side of the lower jaw.

Adding gold ring accents to the tusks...

Now I'm thinking through the mohawk as the creature's signature feature, planning a series of broad blade shapes running along the spine.

Writing path and extrude code...

I'll use a single shared paint function that colors based on absolute y position with threshold mixing, so shorter blades naturally end up less orange at their tips since they're scaled down. Now I'm sweeping that path into a cord shape with a thin radius, then placing pendant items like teeth, claws, and skulls along the path at intervals, figuring out how to position each pendant frame relative to the path's tangent and anchor point.

For the chest-area fetishes, I'm picking the spine joint closest to chest height and attaching shoulder joints as children of the next spine joint up. For a belt, I'm thinking of using a loop centered on the pelvis spine joint, oriented with an upward-facing frame so it wraps naturally around the hips.

For the loincloth, I'm planning hanging flaps extruded from front and back of the belt — flat outlines in the XY plane with a jagged V-shaped bottom edge, tapered thinner near the tip, finished with a painted tribal pattern.

I'm working out where the belt sits by interpolating the torso loft's center z and half-thickness at that height, then casting a ray from the front to find the exact surface hit point and attaching the flap there with a small z offset. The flap hangs down toward y~0.65, which means I need to check it doesn't clip into the thighs since the hips sit at x ±0.27.

Now I'm figuring out the fetish staff for the right hand — a tall painted wooden pole topped with a glowing-eyed skull, feathers, dangling bones and teeth, and a charm with cards, and thinking about how the hand should grip it given the extended-limb rest pose.

Working out finger curl parameters so the staff sits naturally in each hand's grip, with the pole offset forward from the palm and fingers curling around it at a plausible radius.

For shoulder details, I'm adding cheap tusk/bone fetishes on the left pauldron and feathers on the right shoulder, plus a crossed-bone and skull totem bundle on the back. I'm scattering in swamp flavor elements: lily pads, cattails with brown caps, glowing mushrooms, and moss patches via mottled paint, plus a bubbling green voodoo cauldron on a tripod with fire/embers at the rear-left, and a skull-on-stake totem at the back-right, all while watching the part budget stay near 300 and keeping the base radius around 1.4 to stay snug against the troll's arm span and staff.
